name: Modern SEO - M4L4 Pricing Framework with Examples
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-22

Part of: [Modern SEO - Module 4 Client Acquisition and Pricing](lib:brain-modern-seo-module-4-client-acquisition-and-pricing) | [Modern SEO Course](lib:brain-modern-seo-course) | [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

# Summary
Scope-based pricing (4:31): list every delivery step, attach a real cost to each, then add a margin. "Your quote is based on real resource requirements, not arbitrary market rates or what you think clients will pay." No actual prices are shown despite the title.

# Cost components
- **One-time setup:** a Claude project or custom GPT for the client, a client information sheet (business details, target keywords, specs), the GBP audit, the GBP landing page audit, LeadSnap setup. Amortized over the first months; no separate setup fee.
- **Per article:** copywriting (research, writing, editing), schema, AI images, internal and external authority links, an external PBN link (varies by industry and competition), developer publishing, quality control, and updating existing content with internal links to the new article ("often overlooked, but critical").

# Key concepts
- **50 to 70% gross margin**, high because of one-off requests, revisions and feedback outside the base price.
- **Month one:** setup plus about five articles. **Month two onward:** nine a month. Standard projects scale per article (7, 9, 15).
- **Complex projects** (example: 500+ indexed URLs ranking 20+ from the lobby, a Houston plastic surgeon) get custom pricing; estimate technical work separately. "Please do not use the same per article pricing when you're essentially having to rebuild a site's technical foundation."
- **Common mistakes:** ignoring revisions, underestimating technical work, fixed pricing regardless of scope, competing on price.
- **Presenting:** lead with scope and value, then price. Offer good, better, best (low, mid, high), each profitable; margin drops as scale grows.

# Checklist
- Every setup and per-article step costed, including QC and internal link updates.
- 50 to 70% margin; revisions accounted for.
- Month one and month two structure set; technical work priced separately.
- Three profitable options; scope and value before price.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Kim can use the component list to estimate the real effort behind a month of work for [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub), [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) or [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub). TAG's standing items (2 press releases a month, $50 a month for backlinks via [Search Atlas](lib:brain-search-atlas)) fit as cost lines. Pricing is Scott's decision.
- Do not skip internal link updates to older posts on every new blog; consider adding it to [SEO Blog Writing Standards](lib:brain-seo-blog-writing-standards). Updates go to Kim as a copy-paste list (client sites read-only for Claude).
- The QC step matches TAG's setup: Claude drafts, Kim reviews and publishes.
- Alphalete fits the "complex project" pattern (237 mostly programmatic local pages, 3 of 244 indexed per Kim's memory); scope technical work separately from blogs.

# Caveats and open questions
- PBN links are treated as a normal cost and never defined. Confirm with Scott before using them for any client.
- 50 to 70% margin is the instructor's claim. Slide says "profit margin," audio says "gross margin."
- Technical threshold 500 (audio) vs 500+ (slide) vs 450 (M3L1); not firm.
- Examples may be in the written lesson text on the course page; Kim should check. LeadSnap is paid.
